newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian analysts mixed on Aker/RGI merger - poll.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian analysts mixed on Aker/RGI merger - poll.

text.p: Norwegian analysts have mixed opinions about the proposed merger of engineering and offshore company Aker ASA with Resource Group International (RGI), a Reuter poll of five analysts showed on Wednesday.
Two of the analysts said they had downgraded their recommendation on Aker to sell from hold following the merger announcement. Three said they maintained the company as a buy.
Aker and RGI said on Tuesday they had agreed a merger to form a new company Aker RGI ASA, which will concentrate on three business areas -- seafood, cement and oil and gas.
The deal, which values one Aker share at 2.15 RGI shares, is expected to go through in the early part of 1997.
"We don't see that the merger offers Aker shareholders very much, the only shareholder (in Aker) that will benefit is RGI," said one of the analysts.
RGI, the investment group of Norwegian entrepreneur Kjell Inge Roekke, holds 33 percent of Aker and controls 40 percent through options.
All the analysts were agreed that seafoods, RGI's largest business division, was the sector with the most uncertainty.
"RGI has brought two new risk factors into the market that we didn't have to consider before," said another analyst, who was positive to the deal.
"The first is linked to the price of fish, while the second is the political factor to do with fishing quotas."

Another positive analyst said: "The size of the new company means it will be one of the drivers of Norwegian business. It will be able to do what Roekke has always done -- buy cheap, work up and sell at an expensive price. But it will be able to do it on a much larger scale."
